title: Google claims EmbeddingGemma 2 outperforms rival embedding models twice its size
key_facts: Google released EmbeddingGemma 2, an open model that turns text, images, video, audio and code into numerical vectors.
It has 740 million parameters; Google says it is the most compact of its kind and beats models up to twice its size on multimodal embedding benchmarks.
It runs locally without an API key, 20 to 70 ms per query via WebGPU in a browser, using about 191 MB of RAM.
It cuts local vector database storage by up to six times; a 270-million-parameter text-only version exists.
Weights are on Hugging Face and Kaggle.
quote_evidence: At 740 million parameters, Google says it's the most compact model of its kind and outperforms competing models up to twice its size on multimodal embedding benchmarks.
The model runs locally without an API key.
why_it_matters_hint: Small enough to run search over private files on a device without sending data out.
